sources.label: Pro Game Guides - Anime Squadron Tier List
Pro Game Guides - Anime Squadron Beginner's Guide

items.name: Gometa (SSJ4)
items.unlockRoute: Primal Fusion after the Primal Core checklist; requires maxed Goki (SSJ4 Full Power) and Vegata (SSJ4 Full Power).
items.passiveEffect: Stacks damage, defense, dodge, and crit-chance growth from teammate deaths and kills.
items.investmentPriority: Endgame target; plan materials and parent-unit leveling before spending cubes elsewhere.
items.sourceConfidence: Medium - backed by PGG tier/meta notes and Bloxron item-level details; not present on BloxInformer units page.
items.cardSummary: Plan Gometa as the late-game fusion carry, not as a normal banner pull.
items.verificationNote: Included because two independent sources identify the unit and Bloxron provides unlock/passive details. Needs in-game or stronger wiki confirmation during future refresh.
items.bestUse: Long-fight carry for Story, Raids, and Infinite once the account can support the fusion route.

items.name: Woo (Shadow)
items.unlockRoute: Limited banner; available evidence points to an extremely rare chase with a possible pity path.
items.passiveEffect: Skill activation grants a short dodge window and mana generation; kills can convert enemies into Shadow Soldiers.
items.ultimateOrActive: Frenzy Slash spender that uses mana for burst damage.
items.investmentPriority: Only chase after core economy and reliable carry slots are stable.
items.sourceConfidence: Medium - backed by PGG tier/meta notes, Bloxron item-level details, and AnimeSquadronWiki.org unlock notes; not present on BloxInformer units page.
items.cardSummary: A rare limited Secret with ramping shadow-soldier value in longer waves.
items.verificationNote: Keep rate and pity language source-qualified until official/in-game confirmation is available.
items.bestUse: High-damage Infinite or long-wave unit when the player can afford a rare limited chase.

items.name: Madora (Gunbai)
items.unlockRoute: Ninja Village Act 4 boss route, with a low listed drop chance.
items.passiveEffect: Skill attacks apply Burn, and chakra overdrive improves damage and cooldown pressure.
items.investmentPriority: Strong farm target when repeat boss clears are more realistic than banner luck.
items.sourceConfidence: Medium - backed by PGG tier/role placement, Bloxron item-level details, RoboLibrary naming context, and AnimeSquadronWiki.org unlock notes.
items.cardSummary: A farmable Secret burn unit for raid and boss damage checks.
items.verificationNote: Name spelling differs across sources; dataset uses PGG/Bloxron spelling.
items.bestUse: Boss-health pressure and raid fights where damage over time matters.

items.name: Shanron (Omega)
items.unlockRoute: Ultimate Evil Raid, with better odds on normal clears than hard-mode clears.
items.passiveEffect: Deals extra boss damage and rotates elemental modes that add corruption, damage-over-time, or movement-slow pressure.
items.investmentPriority: High for raid accounts, but delay on fresh accounts until economy can support it.
items.sourceConfidence: Medium - backed by PGG tier/role placement, Bloxron item-level details, RoboLibrary naming context, and AnimeSquadronWiki.org unlock notes.
items.cardSummary: A raid-focused Secret built around boss damage and corruption utility.
items.verificationNote: Name spelling differs across sources; dataset uses PGG/Bloxron spelling.
items.bestUse: Raid and boss-focused teams, especially after Maximum Yen upgrades can handle the deploy cost.

items.name: Puppeteer (Transcendent)
items.unlockRoute: Evolve Puppeteer using Katakara challenge materials.
items.passiveEffect: Amplifies self damage and reduces incoming damage during active skill windows.
items.investmentPriority: High-end evolution target after the account has economy and one main carry.
items.sourceConfidence: Medium - backed by PGG tier/meta notes and Bloxron item-level details; not present on BloxInformer units page.
items.cardSummary: A resource-heavy evolved Secret that mixes frontline survival with wide AOE damage.
items.verificationNote: PGG says Puppeteer was a release-version meta addition; keep freshness note for Update 0.5 checks.
items.bestUse: Stable long-run carry when a team needs both damage and frontline durability.

items.name: Rizzuto (Sage)
items.passiveEffect: Builds a charge meter that can grant damage and defense aura bonuses to Nature-type allies.
items.investmentPriority: Good after Maximum Yen improves early deployment timing.
items.sourceConfidence: Medium - backed by PGG ranked roster/role and Bloxron item-level details; not present on BloxInformer units page.
items.cardSummary: A support DPS that rewards stable lanes and Nature-focused setups.
items.bestUse: Boss and mid-game damage support when the front line can keep aura setup stable.

items.name: Vegata (SSJ4 Full Power)
items.unlockRoute: Gacha, then awaken from base Vegata into the SSJ4 Full Power form.
items.passiveEffect: Galick Gun barrage scales with wave count and attack speed.
items.investmentPriority: Worth leveling even after it stops being the main lane carry because it feeds the fusion plan.
items.sourceConfidence: Medium - backed by PGG ranked roster/role, Bloxron item-level details, RoboLibrary naming context, and AnimeSquadronWiki.org fusion notes.
items.cardSummary: A Legendary fusion parent that can still carry mid-game lanes.
items.verificationNote: PGG uses Vegata SSJ4 in the ranked list; Bloxron uses SSJ4 Full Power.
items.bestUse: Mid-game carry and required parent for the Gometa fusion route.

items.name: Goki (SSJ4 Full Power)
items.unlockRoute: Gacha, then awaken to SSJ4 with Eclipse God Stone and Gold.
items.passiveEffect: Below half HP, gains damage, ability damage, and lifesteal; also functions as a true anti-air path for flyer lanes.
items.investmentPriority: High because it solves anti-air pressure and feeds the late-game fusion path.
items.sourceConfidence: High - BloxInformer confirms a Goki SSJ4 unit/passive, while PGG and Bloxron back role and progression value.
items.cardSummary: The SSJ4 Goki line is both anti-air coverage and half of the Gometa plan.
items.verificationNote: BloxInformer uses the shorter label Goki (SSJ4); Bloxron uses Goki (SSJ4 Full Power).
items.bestUse: Flyer lanes, mid-game damage, and required parent for Gometa fusion.

items.name: Shinks
items.passiveEffect: Gives nearby allies defensive support through damage reduction and dodge help.
items.investmentPriority: Useful when a team has damage but needs wave control and survival help.
items.sourceConfidence: Medium - backed by PGG ranked roster/role, Bloxron item-level details, and RoboLibrary naming context; not present on BloxInformer units page.
items.cardSummary: A support unit for protecting the main lane while carries ramp.
items.bestUse: Defensive support slot that buys time for upgrades and carry setup.

items.name: Rudaus
items.passiveEffect: Reduces his own ability cooldown and gives nearby allies a smaller ability-cooldown reduction.
items.investmentPriority: Test with the main DPS first; cooldown support is strongest when the carry benefits from it.
items.sourceConfidence: High - BloxInformer confirms rarity/passive, and PGG/Bloxron support the utility role.
items.cardSummary: A cooldown support unit for skill-heavy teams.
items.verificationNote: BloxInformer lists Epic rarity; Bloxron describes Mythic support. Keep rarity conflict visible in future review.
items.bestUse: Cooldown support for lineups that depend on frequent skill casts.

items.name: Mamosa
items.passiveEffect: Allies in range regenerate HP based on Mamosa's max HP.
items.investmentPriority: Good temporary support; do not over-invest once boss damage outpaces healing.
items.sourceConfidence: High - BloxInformer confirms rarity/passive, and PGG/Bloxron support the healer role.
items.cardSummary: A healer that helps early lanes survive before endgame burst becomes the wall.
items.bestUse: Early and mid-game protection while players learn Acts and stabilize lanes.

items.name: Shield Hero
items.unlockRoute: Unlock path needs confirmation; listed paths include Battle Pass and gacha/campaign availability.
items.passiveEffect: Redirects or intercepts part of the damage aimed at allies.
items.investmentPriority: Good practical tank before late-game fusion options are ready.
items.sourceConfidence: Medium - backed by PGG and Bloxron item-level notes, plus AnimeSquadronWiki.org top-unit guidance; not present on BloxInformer units page.
items.cardSummary: A practical tank choice while building toward stronger endgame options.
items.verificationNote: Unlock route conflicts between PGG and Bloxron; keep source-qualified until checked in-game.
items.bestUse: Frontline survival slot for raids or stages where chip damage threatens the back line.

items.name: Big Beard
items.passiveEffect: Missing HP increases Defense up to a cap.
items.investmentPriority: Low-to-medium; useful early, but not a primary endgame target.
items.sourceConfidence: High - BloxInformer confirms rarity/passive, and PGG/Bloxron support tank value.
items.cardSummary: A bruiser-style tank whose value comes from surviving at lower HP.
items.verificationNote: BloxInformer labels it Mythic; PGG places it as a B-tier tank.
items.bestUse: Temporary bruiser or tank slot until stronger survival units are available.

items.name: Fastwagon
items.passiveEffect: Increases money generation while alive and grants extra Yen on death.
items.investmentPriority: High for new accounts because income is harder to replace than raw damage.
items.sourceConfidence: High - BloxInformer confirms rarity/passive, and PGG/Bloxron both identify the economy role.
items.cardSummary: The dedicated Yen unit for speeding up deployments and upgrades.
items.verificationNote: BloxInformer lists Epic rarity; Bloxron describes Legendary economy. Keep rarity conflict visible in future review.
items.bestUse: Economy slot that helps expensive units come online earlier during waves.

items.name: Karashi (Sharingan)
items.passiveEffect: Marked targets take faster follow-up hits and added crit pressure.
items.investmentPriority: Worth using when pulled early; lower priority than the main endgame carry path.
items.sourceConfidence: Medium - backed by PGG ranked roster/role and Bloxron item-level details; not present on BloxInformer units page.
items.cardSummary: A speed-clear unit for farming lower-pressure stages quickly.
items.bestUse: Fast Act clearing and speed farming before enemy HP scales too high.

items.name: Zemitsu
items.passiveEffect: Periodically enters Sleep Mode for damage, cooldown, and ability-cooldown boosts.
items.investmentPriority: Good early pull, but stop heavy investment once better DPS arrives.
items.sourceConfidence: High - BloxInformer confirms rarity/passive, and PGG/Bloxron support early speed value.
items.cardSummary: A fast early DPS that falls off once stronger damage units arrive.
items.verificationNote: BloxInformer lists Epic rarity; Bloxron describes Common speed DPS.
items.bestUse: Early speed-clear slot before stronger Mythic or Legendary DPS units replace it.

items.name: Ramuru
items.passiveEffect: Kills absorb Max HP into Ramuru's damage up to a cap.
items.investmentPriority: Low; use briefly and recycle or bench after stronger pulls.
items.sourceConfidence: High - BloxInformer confirms rarity/passive, and PGG/Bloxron support early-filler value.
items.cardSummary: A starter-friendly DPS filler with limited long-term scaling.
items.verificationNote: BloxInformer spells this Ramuru; keep that spelling for now.
items.bestUse: Cheap early DPS filler until higher-tier units take the lane.

items.name: Choi
items.passiveEffect: Simple combo chain without meaningful scaling hooks.
items.investmentPriority: Low; replace at the first reliable B-tier or better pull.
items.sourceConfidence: Medium - backed by PGG ranked roster/role and Bloxron item-level details; not present on BloxInformer units page.
items.cardSummary: A low-priority early DPS placeholder.
items.bestUse: Early Act body when the player needs any lane filled.

items.name: Tranks
items.passiveEffect: Melee crits can briefly stun nearby targets.
items.investmentPriority: Low; do not carry it into raid progression unless roster options are thin.
items.sourceConfidence: Medium - backed by PGG ranked roster/role and Bloxron item-level details; not present on BloxInformer units page.
items.cardSummary: A filler hybrid whose brief crit stun is useful only while options are limited.
items.bestUse: Temporary hybrid filler in early or mid Acts.

items.name: Zaro
items.passiveEffect: Ability attacks apply Bleed that damages over time and reduces regeneration.
items.ultimateOrActive: Executioner resets ability cooldown after a kill, with a cooldown.
items.investmentPriority: Low-to-medium; useful early, but do not over-invest for endgame.
items.sourceConfidence: High - BloxInformer confirms rarity/passive, and PGG/Bloxron support early-filler value.
items.cardSummary: A bleed-focused DPS that works early but is not a long-term carry.
items.verificationNote: PGG places Zaro low despite BloxInformer listing a Legendary passive.
items.bestUse: Early lane DPS with bleed utility before better units replace it.

items.name: Shin
items.passiveEffect: Ability attacks apply Burn, and repeated ability casts stack extra Burn damage up to a cap.
items.investmentPriority: Low; replace when stronger burn or burst units arrive.
items.sourceConfidence: High - BloxInformer confirms rarity/passive, and PGG lists Shin in the ranked roster.
items.cardSummary: A burn-based early DPS that should be replaced by stronger carries.
items.verificationNote: BloxInformer lists Legendary rarity; Bloxron text extraction around Shin was inconsistent, so BloxInformer/PGG are weighted more heavily.
items.bestUse: Early DPS filler when burn pressure helps basic progression.

items.name: Igras
items.passiveEffect: Weak dagger attacks with no meaningful scaling hook.
items.investmentPriority: Very low; avoid Stat Cube spending.
items.sourceConfidence: Medium - backed by PGG ranked roster/role and Bloxron item-level details; not present on BloxInformer units page.
items.cardSummary: A starter unit to replace before any serious reroll spending.
items.bestUse: Starter body for the first pulls and first lanes.

items.name: Michigo
items.passiveEffect: At half HP, gains Speed and Damage until death.
items.investmentPriority: Very low; recycle or bench after better pulls.
items.sourceConfidence: High - BloxInformer confirms rarity/passive, and PGG/Bloxron support low-tier filler value.
items.cardSummary: A low-priority DPS filler with a half-HP self-buff.
items.bestUse: Low-ceiling filler when no better lane unit is available.

items.name: Asto
items.passiveEffect: Takes reduced ability damage.
items.investmentPriority: Very low; do not spend major reroll items.
items.sourceConfidence: High - BloxInformer confirms rarity/passive, and PGG/Bloxron support low-tier filler value.
items.cardSummary: A short-term filler whose defensive passive does not justify long-term investment.
items.bestUse: Temporary early body with a defensive passive.

items.name: Goki
items.passiveEffect: Every third attack gains extra ability damage.
items.investmentPriority: Low for combat, but keep progression needs in mind if pursuing Goki SSJ4 and Gometa.
items.sourceConfidence: High - BloxInformer confirms rarity/passive, and PGG/Bloxron support low-tier base-form value.
items.cardSummary: Base Goki is mainly useful as a stepping stone toward stronger forms.
items.bestUse: Base-form stepping stone toward the SSJ4 line, not a long-term carry.

items.name: Mab
items.passiveEffect: Every third attack deals extra damage.
items.investmentPriority: Very low; replace quickly.
items.sourceConfidence: High - BloxInformer confirms rarity/passive, and PGG/Bloxron support low-tier filler value.
items.cardSummary: A simple early DPS filler with every-third-attack damage.
items.bestUse: Early roster body while waiting for stronger DPS.

items.name: Muffy
items.passiveEffect: Gains a base Dodge chance.
items.investmentPriority: Very low; never a priority cube target.
items.sourceConfidence: High - BloxInformer confirms rarity/passive, and PGG/Bloxron support low-tier filler value.
items.cardSummary: A low-priority brawler whose dodge passive is not enough for long-term investment.
items.bestUse: Early filler when the roster is still thin.
